biomarker_name.notes: Multiple biomarkers identified in the study related to T1DM; some are human proteins (pancreatic enzymes, immune proteins) and others are microbial taxa/genes

biomarker_unit.evidence_quote: Relative protein abundances of human AMY2A and AMY2B; transcript levels; mOTU-based taxonomic profiles; relative abundances of metagenomic operational taxonomic units

biomarker_unit.notes: Units vary by biomarker type: proteins measured as relative abundance %, microbial taxa as mOTU abundance %

feces_phenotype_value.evidence_quote: In most cases, mOTU-based taxonomic profiles were stable over time within individuals. Given that family members share environment, nutrition and genetic background, families formed more distinct groups than unrelated individuals, and samples did not cluster according to T1DM status
feces_phenotype_value.section: Results — Study cohort and microbial community structures
feces_phenotype_value.notes: Fecal phenotype characterized by metagenomic composition; primary finding is strong family effect overriding T1DM status

value: Study cohort: 20 individuals from 4 families with multiple T1DM cases across 2+ generations
T1DM diagnosed >5 years, controlled by insulin replacement therapy
Healthy relatives had no immediate risk of T1DM based on auto-antibody status
Metaproteomic data: 185,000 ± 13,000 peptide mass spectra per sample
36 of 53 samples subjected to multi-omic analysis from 18 individuals
Blood analytics included islet cell antibodies, insulin antibodies, GAD2 antibodies, ZnT8 antibodies
Thiamine levels measured in plasma from subset of participants
Integrated multi-omic workflow used: co-assembly of metagenomic and metatranscriptomic reads
Binned genomes: 200 population-level genomes with >93% completeness
De novo assembly: 287 ± 43 Mbp total contig length, N50: 660 ± 130 bp
2,400 ± 1,600 microbial and 200 ± 70 human protein groups identified per sample
Non-human eukaryotic genes: 0.07 ± 0.05% of metagenomic reads, 0.8 ± 1% of metatranscriptomic reads, 2.6 ± 3.1% of identified proteins
Viral biomolecules: <0.1% of predicted ORFs, mappable reads, and identified proteins
